TTGR42 – West Fife Villages 3

Start: Dalgety Bay Sailing Club · Finish: Dalgety Bay Sailing Club

Distance: 47.9 miles · Ascent: approx. 0 m · Descent: approx. 0 m · Difficulty: Moderately Difficult

Route map and gradients

Showing the normal route map.

Scenery and points of interest

Starting from Dalgety Bay Sailing Club, this varied 47.9-mile circular ride explores an extensive collection of villages and communities across western and central Fife. Heading inland through Crossgates and Hill of Beath, the route continues towards Kelty, Lumphinnans and Lochgelly before passing through Glencraig, Crosshill and Lochore. This northern section takes riders through an area closely associated with Fife's mining heritage, where established communities sit among the rolling countryside.

From Lochore, the journey turns back through Kelty and continues towards Kingseat, Townhill and Bowershall. The route then explores the countryside around Muirside and Craigluscar before reaching Crossford and Cairneyhill. This middle section offers a changing mixture of village surroundings, rural landscapes and gentle hills, giving pilots and stokers plenty of variety as they make their way across western Fife.

The final part of the circuit heads towards Torryburn and Crombie before continuing through Charleston and Limekilns, bringing the ride back towards the shores of the Firth of Forth. The coastal communities provide a pleasing contrast to the inland villages encountered earlier in the day. From Limekilns, the route returns through Rosyth and Inverkeithing to Dalgety Bay Sailing Club, completing a substantial and satisfying tour of western Fife.

Route highlights
  • Crossgates and Hill of Beath: The opening journey inland from Dalgety Bay towards central Fife.
  • Lochgelly, Glencraig and Crosshill: Communities reflecting the area's long association with coal mining.
  • Lochore: A village near Lochore Meadows Country Park, marking the northern section of the circuit.
  • Kingseat and Townhill: A transition towards the countryside around Dunfermline.
  • Muirside and Craigluscar: Rural locations providing a contrast to the larger settlements along the route.
  • Torryburn, Charleston and Limekilns: Communities close to the Firth of Forth, adding a coastal dimension to the final part of the ride.

Terrain and cycling difficulty

Difficulty: Moderately Difficult

West Fife Villages 3 is a rewarding 47.9-mile circular ride combining the rolling countryside of central Fife with an extended tour of its villages and coastal communities. Although the overall climbing is relatively modest for the distance, the length of the circuit and repeated changes in elevation make steady pacing and good teamwork important.

  • Distance: Approximately 47.9 miles (77.1 km), starting and finishing at Dalgety Bay Sailing Club. This is a substantial outing, so allow plenty of time for rest stops, refreshments and regrouping.
  • Climbing: Approximately 285 metres of cumulative ascent are estimated. The route climbs away from the low-lying Forth coast towards the higher ground around Hill of Beath and Kelty, with further undulations through the inland sections.
  • Descending: Around 285 metres of cumulative descent are estimated. The later stages generally return towards lower elevations around Torryburn, Charleston and Limekilns, although smaller climbs and descents occur throughout.
  • Gradients: Elevations range from approximately 6 to 165 metres above sea level. Some shorter uphill sections may approach 5%, requiring timely gear selection and a comfortable, coordinated pedalling rhythm.
  • Route character: The circuit passes through numerous villages and towns, with frequent changes of direction as it links Lochgelly, Lochore, Kingseat, Townhill, Crossford, Cairneyhill and the Forth-side communities. Pilots should anticipate junctions and village approaches, maintaining clear communication with their stokers.
  • Tandem considerations: The main challenge is likely to be the combination of distance and repeated smaller climbs rather than any single major ascent. A sustainable pace, regular opportunities to rest and clear communication before junctions, descents and changes in direction will help make the ride comfortable and enjoyable for both riders.

Overall: A varied and satisfying moderately difficult ride, offering an extended exploration of western Fife's villages, countryside and coastal communities. Particularly suited to tandem teams comfortable with longer distances who enjoy discovering the different characters of Fife's local communities.
